claims.explanation: Dofetilide is a potent blocker of the hERG (KCNH2) potassium channel, and its selective antiproliferative effect across cancer lines likely reflects dependence on KCNH2/hERG expression or activity for proliferation and survival. Lines with high KCNH2 expression or channel-addicted states (e.g., via EGF/KRAS/MAPK-driven tumors) are sensitized, while lines with low KCNH2 expression or compensatory potassium channel expression are protected. The observed enrichment of TP53, KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and PTEN mutations in sensitive lines suggests that oncogenic signaling and loss of tumor suppressors may upregulate hERG or increase dependence on its function.

features.basis: hERG is the primary target of dofetilide; high expression increases drug block and dependence
Compensatory potassium channel expression may bypass hERG blockade
Alternative inward rectifier may maintain potassium homeostasis when hERG is blocked
Background potassium leak channel may compensate for loss of hERG current
TP53 mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, possibly linking to altered potassium channel regulation
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may drive hERG dependence via MAPK signaling
EGFR mutations in sensitive lung lines may upregulate hERG or increase dependence
BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma and other lines may promote hERG expression
PTEN loss in sensitive lines may enhance PI3K/AKT-driven hERG activity
ARID1A mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, suggesting context-dependent or weak effect
PIK3CA mutations in some sensitive lines may contribute to hERG upregulation
CTNNB1 mutations are common in resistant lines, possibly indicating reduced hERG dependence
